# Draft:Shnyar Anwar__disambig_1

----
Shnyar Anwar is a Kurdish-American politician and a Member of the Sixth Term of the Kurdistan Parliament, representing the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK). She took her parliamentary oath on 2 December 2024 in Erbil. Shnyar Anwar is noted for a public-service model commonly described as “MP Beyond Parliament Walls,” characterized by regular field visits, direct engagement with residents, and continuous follow-up on local issues outside formal parliamentary duties. Her model often described as “MP Beyond Parliament Walls” (MPB) marks the first documented instance in the Kurdistan Parliament of an elected member conducting a large-scale, continuous service mission outside the parliamentary building. This approach is characterized by direct engagement, problem-solving, and practical support delivered through community visits, youth initiatives, development projects, and local follow-up operations.
Over the course of her first eight months in office (from December 2, 2024), MP Shnyar Anwar completed projects and visits that reached over 34,000 direct beneficiaries and nearly 70,000 indirect beneficiaries. Her initiatives include educational support programs, sustainable development installations, training courses for youth, community-based assistance for vulnerable groups, and ongoing neighborhood-level problem-solving efforts. These projects were implemented independently, outside the scope of formal parliamentary mechanisms, and represent a unique model of public service not previously established in Kurdistan’s parliamentary history.
Election and Parliamentary Work
Shnyar Anwar was elected to the Kurdistan Parliament in 2024 as a candidate of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan. After assuming office, she participated in legislative duties while also developing a service model focused on practical community involvement.
Public Service Beyond Parliament
Field Engagement and Casework
During her first year in office, Shnyar Anwar conducted extensive visits to districts, villages, institutions, schools, and community centers to meet residents and gather concerns. Over this period, she completed a documented total of 145 public transactions and cases, including administrative follow-ups and assistance with individual and community issues.
Thankfulness Campaign
Shortly after taking the parliamentary oath, Shnyar Anwar launched a post-election thankfulness campaign. She revisited locations she had engaged with during her election campaign to express appreciation and maintain communication with local communities. This was noted as an early example of a structured post-election outreach effort by an MP in the Kurdistan Region.
Youth Meetings and Idea Development
Shnyar Anwar holds weekly meetings with young people who present ideas, proposals, and community-based projects. Many of these initiatives were later developed into training programs, volunteer activities, and small-scale community projects facilitated through her office.
Projects and Community Initiatives
During her early months in office, Shnyar Anwar’s activities reached more than 34,000 direct beneficiaries and nearly 70,000 indirect beneficiaries. Her work included support programs for school communities, training courses for youth, volunteer-driven initiatives, and assistance to vulnerable and minority groups. Her office organized ten free training courses and collaborated with approximately one hundred volunteers in community-service activities.
Sustainable Development Efforts
Shnyar Anwar supported the installation of several solar-energy units in educational and public institutions, including universities and health centers. These installations served a substantial number of indirect beneficiaries and were noted as part of her broader focus on sustainable community support.
Public-Service Approach
Shnyar Anwar’s model of work integrates parliamentary representation with field-based service, emphasizing presence in communities, direct communication, follow-up on issues, youth development, volunteer engagement, and localized problem-solving. This combined approach has been described in local documentation as a structured example of public service beyond the formal boundaries of parliament.
